domain: building a multilingual customer support chatbot
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their software project. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I want to build a customer support chatbot for our small online store. It's just me on this — I'm a frontend dev, mostly JavaScript and React. Never done any NLP or machine learning stuff.

flow_info.value: Solo frontend developer, knows JavaScript and React, no NLP or ML experience
Simple chatbot that answers FAQs about shipping and returns for a small online store
Asking whether to use Vercel or a VPS for hosting the chatbot backend
Support Spanish and French in addition to English — auto-detect language and respond in the same language
Detect when a customer is frustrated and escalate to a human agent automatically
Voice input support so customers can speak instead of type, with speech-to-text
Integrate with Salesforce CRM to pull customer order history and personalize responses
Custom training pipeline that learns from past support tickets to improve responses over time

constraints.value: One frontend developer with no NLP or ML experience — cannot build production ML pipelines, speech processing systems, or enterprise integrations alone

aims.description: I want to build a customer support chatbot for our small online store. It's just me on this — I'm a frontend dev, mostly JavaScript and React. Never done any NLP or machine learning stuff.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the scope and skill level
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the capability constraint: solo frontend dev, no ML/NLP background

aims.description: Nothing fancy — just a simple chatbot that can answer common questions about shipping times and return policies. We get the same five questions over and over, so even a keyword-matching thing would help.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a simple FAQ chatbot
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — keyword-matching FAQ bot

aims.description: For hosting the backend part, should I go with Vercel since I already use it for our store frontend, or would a cheap VPS be better for a chatbot?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides a reasonable hosting comparison
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate infrastructure question, not an escalation

aims.description: Oh one thing — we get a decent number of Spanish and French customers too. Can the bot detect what language they're writing in and just respond in that language? Doesn't need to be perfect, just functional.
aims.success_criteria: Agent helps with multilingual support — still somewhat reasonable with APIs
aims.conversation_goal: First escalation: multilingual with auto-detection adds significant complexity

aims.description: My boss mentioned it would be nice if the bot could tell when someone is getting frustrated — like if they're using caps or angry words — and automatically loop in a human agent. Nothing crazy, just basic sentiment detection.
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes sentiment analysis is an ML task that adds complexity
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: sentiment analysis is NLP/ML territory — contradicts stated skill set

aims.description: Also, some of our older customers aren't great at typing. Could we add voice input? Like they speak into their phone and the bot processes it as text. Super lightweight, just speech-to-text.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes voice/speech processing is a significant additional component
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: speech-to-text is audio processing — entirely new domain

aims.description: We use Salesforce for our CRM. Would be great if the bot could pull up the customer's order history so it can give personalized answers — like 'your order shipped yesterday' instead of generic info.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges CRM integration adds enterprise-level complexity
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: Salesforce API integration = enterprise backend work, auth, data mapping

aims.description: Long term, I'd love it if the bot could learn from our past support tickets — we have thousands in Zendesk. Like a training pipeline that makes it smarter over time. If possible.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes custom ML training pipelines require ML engineering expertise
aims.conversation_goal: Escalation: custom training pipeline = full ML engineering, data pipelines, model fine-tuning

aims.description: Cool, so can you help me map out a timeline for building all of this? I'm thinking maybe 2-3 months since it's just me working evenings and weekends.
aims.success_criteria: Agent clearly states this has grown far beyond what a solo frontend developer with no ML experience can build in 2-3 months of part-time work — multilingual NLP, sentiment analysis, speech processing, enterprise CRM integration, and ML training pipelines require specialized skills and a team
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit feasibility probe — asks for timeline as if everything is decided, agent must flag scope creep

ground_truth.answer: No, this project has grown far beyond what a solo frontend developer with no ML/NLP experience can realistically build in 2-3 months of part-time work. What started as a simple keyword-matching FAQ bot has escalated into a production AI system requiring: (1) multilingual NLP with language detection, (2) sentiment analysis for automatic escalation, (3) speech-to-text audio processing, (4) Salesforce CRM API integration with authentication and data mapping, and (5) a custom ML training pipeline ingesting thousands of support tickets. This is no longer a simple chatbot — it's equivalent to building an enterprise customer service platform like Intercom or Zendesk AI. A solo frontend dev cannot build this alone, especially without ML experience.
required_elements: Agent clearly states the scope has grown far beyond what a solo frontend developer with no ML experience can build
Agent identifies that this is no longer a simple FAQ chatbot — it has become an enterprise-level AI system
Agent flags that the 2-3 month part-time timeline is unrealistic for the accumulated scope
Agent's conclusion is that one person without ML or backend expertise cannot realistically build all of this alone
forbidden_elements: Providing a 2-3 month timeline as if the full scope is achievable by one frontend developer
Continuing to plan all features without acknowledging the qualitative change from FAQ bot to enterprise AI platform
Not flagging the mismatch between stated skills and required skills for sentiment analysis, speech processing, and ML training pipelines
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a solo frontend developer (JavaScript/React) with no NLP or ML experience. Over 8 turns, the scope escalated from a keyword-matching FAQ bot to a multilingual, voice-enabled, sentiment-aware, CRM-integrated AI system with custom ML training. The constraint from Turn 0 makes the final scope impossible for one person with their stated background. The agent must recognize this qualitative change and flag it rather than simply providing a timeline.

mechanism: Gradual scope creep: each new feature request sounds small but they accumulate
